name: Tango
subcategory: screen recording, walkthroughs and product demos
tagline: Capture a workflow and generate a concise step guide with screenshots and annotations

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 5 shared workflows; browser capture; up to 10 users/workspace

tiers.name: Pro Personal
tiers.limits: 1–2 paid users; unlimited workflows; 14-day version history
tiers.notes: The supplied snapshot said $24/month for Pro; the current Personal rate is $26 monthly or $22/month annually.

tiers.name: Pro Team
tiers.limits: 3+ paid users; unlimited workflows; 14-day version history

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom users, security and support; 365-day version history
tiers.notes: Enterprise also charges a platform fee based on users supported.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 shared workflows, browser capture and up to 10 users in the workspace
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; Pro pricing is per paid user
pricing.hiddenCosts: Every Pro user is billable; Enterprise adds a platform fee based on the number of users supported.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Tango, capture a workflow and generate a concise step guide with screenshots and annotations. The hard boundary is browser and desktop capture, blur controls, team sharing, and integrations, plus capture polish, hosting, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Capture a screen workflow with microphone audio, trim the result, annotate key moments, generate a concise step guide with screenshots, and export a shareable local video.
whatYouLose: browser and desktop capture, blur controls, team sharing, and integrations
ongoingBurden: OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Tango because the recording itself is easy; the subscription removes upload, transcoding, sharing, organization, and support work. The recurring cost buys OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Cap
priorArt.desc: Open-source screen recording and sharing product with modern desktop architecture.

alternatives.name: Mimik
alternatives.desc: Tango without the cloud: click through a workflow and get local, editable steps.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal desktop recorder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Tango in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, ffmpeg, and SQLite; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: capture a screen workflow with microphone audio, trim the result, annotate key moments, generate a concise step guide with screenshots, and export a shareable local video.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Offer screen, window, or region capture plus optional microphone audio.
Show an always-visible recording timer and make stop available from the tray.
Create a non-destructive trim view with crop, zoom, cursor highlight, and text callouts.
Render locally through ffmpeg with sensible H.264 and WebM presets.
Generate a poster frame, transcript, and Markdown summary beside each video.
Provide copy-file-path and reveal-in-folder actions instead of mandatory cloud upload.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out public cloud hosting.
Deliberately leave out viewer identity and engagement analytics.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workspaces and SSO.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
